Reach

Who this class is for

So much advice online. So little of it explained.

  • Women who want to understand hypothalamic amenorrhea clearly, from a registered dietitian, without the noise.
  • Active women curious about how fuel, rest and stress connect to the menstrual cycle.
  • Partners, friends and practitioners who want to support someone through period recovery.
  • Anyone tired of conflicting posts and forums, who wants the science in plain English.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover live

What HA is, and what it isn’t

What hypothalamic amenorrhea means, why it’s often mistaken for other things, and why a proper medical evaluation always comes first.

How stress, fuel and rest talk to hormones

The science of how the brain reads the body’s signals, explained simply, without numbers, rules or meal plans.

The myths that keep women stuck

The most common pieces of misinformation I hear, and what the research actually says instead.

The five parts of recovery

Why “eat more, move less” is only part of the picture, and how mindset and individual factors fit in.

Keeping your identity

How to think about an active lifestyle and who you are while you focus on recovery, so it never feels like losing yourself.

Meet Cynthia

Hi, I’m Cynthia Donovan

I’m a registered dietitian (MS, RDN) who specialises in period recovery, and the host of The Period Recovery Podcast. Before this was my work, it was my own story: I’ve been through period loss myself.

Through my coaching programme, Recipe for a Period®, I give active women individualised nutrition guidance and support, so recovery doesn’t have to mean giving up who they are.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Why is it $17 and not free?

Because people who invest, even a little, show up and listen properly. I want a room of women who are ready to learn.

Is this a meal plan or a diet?

No. There are no meal plans, no numbers and no rules in this class. It’s education on the science, so you can make sense of what you read and hear.

Is this medical advice?

No. The class is educational content. It doesn’t diagnose anything or replace your doctor or care team. For anything medical, please speak with your own provider.

What if I’m finding food or exercise really hard right now?

You’re welcome in class, and please also reach out to your doctor or an eating disorder professional for support alongside it. You deserve care that’s individual to you.

Can I come if I’m supporting someone else?

Yes. Partners, friends, family and practitioners are very welcome.

What if I can’t make it live?

Save your seat anyway. Every seat includes the full replay.

Will you talk about coaching at the end?

For the last few minutes I’ll share how to apply for Recipe for a Period®, for anyone who wants personalised support. Everything before that is yours either way.
